commits.author: Sanoj Doddapaneni
commits.subject: CI: install Chrome and retry when the debugging port is slow to open
commits.body:
GitHub Actions sometimes failed at npm run build:dist with
"Chrome did not open a debugging port" after a 20-second wait. A
passing run of the same workflow finished measuring in 17 seconds,
so the timeout was too tight, and the script reserved a port then
closed it before handing it to Chrome, which can lose the race.

Install Chrome for Testing in CI and pass it as CHROME_PATH, let
Chrome pick the debug port, wait up to 60 seconds, and retry the
launch three times. The accessibility check uses the same launcher.

checker_problems: 25 files, 1695 insertions — split into one logical change per commit
commits.body:
- GitHub Actions CI: lint, unit tests, and an end-to-end smoke test
  that boots the real service with real embedding/reranker models and
  checks every example document is retrievable.
- Example documents in data/examples/ covering every supported type
  (md, txt, py, pdf, docx, html, csv, json, png, wav, mp4), each about

- scripts/smoke_test.py: the same end-to-end check CI runs, runnable
  locally with 'make smoke'.
- Streamlit GUI in streamlit_app/: Chat, Search, Documents, Health &
  stats tabs as a client of the service API.
- Pin av<19: faster-whisper 1.2.1 passes metadata_errors to av.open,
  which PyAV 19 removed — with av 19 every audio/video file fails
  to index.

commits.author: Sanoj D
commits.subject: Local RAG: enterprise FastAPI service with ChromaDB, hybrid retrieval, and live folder sync
checker_problems: 62 files, 3941 insertions — split into one logical change per commit
commits.body:
- MVC inside app/ (core, models, repositories, services, api/v1)
- Chunkers for text (recursive/section/fixed), code, PDF, Word, HTML,
  CSV/JSON, images (OCR), video/audio (whisper transcription)
- Retrieval: dense (ChromaDB) + BM25 (k1 1.5, b 0.75) fused with RRF k=60,
  cross-encoder reranking, optional MMR
- Folder sync: startup scan with SQLite manifest (SHA-256), live watchdog
  watcher with debounce, manual sync endpoint
- Small local models: bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings, MiniLM-L-6-v2 reranker,
  Ollama + llama3.2:3b generation behind swappable provider interfaces
- 48 pytest tests, ruff clean, live smoke test passed (dummy providers)

commits.author: d-sanoj
commits.subject: v2 step 3: bigger model — val 5.262 → 5.225, complete 68% → 70%, good still 0/50
checker_problems: 16 files, 1125 insertions — split into one logical change per commit
commits.body: One lever, capacity: d_model 128 → 256, 6 layers, 8 heads, context 96 words. Same 40k vocab and 50k jokes as step 2, so only capacity changes. 14,997,504 params, 1,500 steps (~4.4 epochs), val 5.225 (train 4.743), complete 70% (35/50), coherent 4/50, joke-shaped 0/50, good 0/50, <unk> in 9/50 samples, 0 duplicates. Capacity is ruled out as the bottleneck at this scale — 2.5x the parameters bought 0.04 of val loss and zero good jokes; the model learns joke surface, not setup → punchline. Two runtime restarts killed the run (at step 750 and step 1250); it resumed cleanly from the step-500 and step-1000 checkpoints. API default checkpoint is now word-level-50k-big (step 1500), the best so far.

commits.author: d-sanoj
commits.subject: v2 step 1: word-level tokens — complete 4% → 62%, good still 0/50
checker_problems: 13 files, 1088 insertions — split into one logical change per commit
commits.body:
Word-level tokenizer (10k vocab, context 64 words), same 15k jokes,
same-ish model (d_model 128, 4 layers, 2.08M params), 1500 steps.
Val loss 5.026 (train 4.738); complete 31/50 (62%), coherent 3/50,
joke-shaped 0/50, good 0/50, duplicates 0%.

The model learned real words and joke openings, but leans on <unk>
as a filler: 44/50 samples contain <unk>, and the rubric fails any
sample with one on coherence. Even the 6 <unk>-free samples are not
jokes. The <unk> crutch is the blocker for the next steps.

Training was killed by a service restart at step 900; resumed from
the step-500 checkpoint (resume support added). Total wall ~40 min.

commits.author: Sanoj D
commits.subject: v2: judging rubric for good% (locked in before any v2 sample)

commits.author: Sanoj D
commits.subject: v2 infra: word-level tokenizer, top-p decoding, per-config corpus
checker_problems: 11 files, 847 insertions — split into one logical change per commit
commits.body:
Add a word tokenizer (10k most frequent words + <pad>/<unk>/<eos>,
each joke ends with <eos>) alongside the v1 char tokenizer, sharing
one interface so training and generation are tokenizer-agnostic.
Checkpoints now record which tokenizer they use, so generation loads
the right one. Add top-p (nucleus) sampling to generation and the API,
a per-config corpus file override (for the 50k-joke step), and
--sample-n/--out to the corpus cleaner. New v2 driver
scripts/run_v2.py runs one lever at a time and saves 50 samples per
step verbatim for human judging of good%.

Also fixes a real bug the new code exposed: the v1 char vocab has no
newline, so the old stop check (decoded char == newline) could never
fire and samples always ran to max_tokens. A stop_token_id of 0 (the
fallback) is a real token (a space), so it must be None when the stop
token is absent — otherwise generation stops at the first space.

commits.author: d-sanoj
commits.subject: jokeGPT: tiny character-level GPT trained on 15k short jokes
checker_problems: 61 files, 18155 insertions — split into one logical change per commit
commits.body:
Character-level transformer (d_model 128, 4 layers, 4 heads, 819,840
params) trained from scratch on CPU on the Short Jokes dataset
(ysharma/short_jokes, MIT). Main run: 1500 steps, val loss 2.064.

Honest headline: the model learned to spell, not to tell jokes —
only 4% of samples finish as a complete sentence. FINDINGS.md has
the full numbers, the ablations (data size, training length, model
size, temperature), and the best/worst generated jokes verbatim.

FastAPI service (MVC in app/), training as a background job,
generation + experiment endpoints, 13 tests green, ruff clean.
Visuals in visuals/ (loss, ablations, temperature, architecture).
